How we proved it halts

Replaying a counter until a regrouped digit halts it

Left of the head is a counter written in three-cell digits; right of it is a long "bell", a row of 001 blocks with one odd block, 0001, inside. Each round, the head adds 1 to the counter, walks out to the odd block and moves it one block closer to the counter. When it arrives, the bell bites a few cells off the counter's low end, and the odd block starts over near the bell's far end: one cycle.

The key idea: most rounds are plain counting. On digits whose middle cell is 0 ("clean" digits), a round adds 1 in base 4, each digit standing for −1, 0, 1 or 2, so long stretches of rounds reduce to arithmetic. The surprises come from bites: a bite usually removes a number of cells that is not a multiple of 3, so the remaining cells regroup into new digits, each made of the end of one old digit and the start of the next. That can create "dirty" digits (middle cell 1), which counting never makes and later carries usually clean up.

Why it halts: the machine stops when a carry reaches a dirty 110 while the next higher digit ends in 1. Over 611,578 cycles, a 110 or 111 appears right after a bite only 369 times, and only in the last cycle does the next higher digit end in 1. There a carry turns the 111 into 110 (round 3,339), and the next carry to reach it (round 7,435) hits the missing instruction. Summing exact per-cycle step formulas, in three independent counts, gives about 1.8 quintillion steps (1,816,824,067,232,869,945).

In Rocq (busycoq), clean rounds are proved lemmas applied in batches, and all other rounds run on a verified simulator. A checker, proved correct once, replays the run from step 288 in 4,942,483 checked moves; this proves halting, not the step count.

Mechanism

What to check here: the pictures show the mechanism that the rule table describes.

How it works: 3 notes
  • Round start K(w,b,c) = 0^inf w 0 E> 101 (001)^b 0001 (001)^c 0^inf; w = 3-cell digits x0y worth 2x-y (001=-1, 000=0, 101=1, 100=2). Round (b>=3): K(w,b,c) -> K(w+1,b-1,c+1) in 12b+22+14t(+4) steps, exact, 300/300.
  • Eat (b=2): 1-7 sub-rounds over the bell; the boundary moves left d = 3j+2 cells (pure bite for d>=5), b' = c+1..c+5, so L grows ~1-3 per eat and L ~ step^(1/3). The 2-cell alignment shift leaves dirty digits 010/011, which later carries clean.
  • Halting routes exist (round on ...1 110; eat on a 111 top, fed by eats on 011 tops), but to 3e10 steps (1,597 eats) no pre-eat counter has a 011/111 top: avoidance looks structural, as in W4-2. No closed form for the eat yet.

different table (not a near neighbour); same architecture as our W4-2 kill (BECv5 TM1/TM2 plus an invariant)
note
BECv5/W4-2: K(w,n,m) = w <A 1 (10)^(1+n) 0 (10)^m, bounce n-1, m+1, w -> phi(w) (binary +1); overflow at n = 0 bites q+1 trailing cells, parity of q decides safety. Here: the same bounce rule with a signed base-4 counter on 3-cell digits, the overflow is a multi-sub-round eat at b = 2 that bites d = 3j+2 cells and re-aligns the digits, and halting needs a dirty top digit (011/111) under a deep bite. RIncs/LIncs-style lemmas carry over in shape; the eat and the dirty-digit tracking are new.
Proof strategy & riskshow the formal proof will go · 3 risks to watch

1) Derive the eat exactly: the left E-run through the low digits and the B sub-rounds over the bell, giving d = 3j+2 and w' from w's low digits. 2) Abstract simulator on (w,b,c), checked against direct simulation. 3) Look for a W4-2-style invariant: dirty high digits are cleaned by carries before a bite deep enough to reach them.

  • ▲The path to the halting cycle (1.82e18 steps) is not directly simulated; it rests on the cycle model (eat bell-size independence, round b-independence, clean-increment arithmetic), checked on all 611,577 eats, ~2.0M oracle rounds, 1,572 direct cycles and 22,905 independently recomputed cycles.
  • ▲A Rocq certificate needs parametric eat/round lemmas for this table and a checked replay of 611,577 cycles (C2-552 style); effort is large but mechanical.
  • ▲No exact total step count yet (dominant term 1.8168e18).
